purpose: Original 3D model of the BBC micro:bit V2 board at true size, with separable parts (A and B buttons with caps, touch logo, 25 individually lit LEDs, edge connector with five pin rings, and the back-side components) so Studio can orbit it and drive A, B, logo and LEDs by part_id. Educational stand-in for the MakeCode simulator board; no logos, FCC ID or silkscreen text.

provenance.author: GuateGeeks
provenance.origin: Original model from the official hardware specification; photos used as reference only. Board outline checked against https://tech.microbit.org/hardware/2-2-revision/ (V2.2: 51.60 mm x 42.00 mm x 11.65 mm incl. components; button 4.55 mm, speaker 3.00 mm and JST socket 5.50 mm above the board) under the hardware overview https://tech.microbit.org/hardware/. The spec pages give no PCB thickness (1.6 mm assumed) or component coordinates: those are estimated from reference photos and remain unconfirmed.

blockoutChecks: The 25 LED volumes form a regular 5 x 5 grid centred left-right on the board, each readable as its own small block.
Button A sits to the left of the LED grid and button B to the right, at about the same height as the grid, both clearly raised above the board.
The touch logo plate sits above (toward the USB edge) the LED grid, centred left-right.
The five pin rings read left to right as 0, 1, 2, 3V, GND along the lower (edge connector) edge, with the gold finger strip below them.

Seen from the back, the USB connector, reset button and battery socket sit along the top edge, with the speaker near the board centre and the microphone and other components distinguishable as separate volumes.
The board is a thin flat plate of about 52 x 42 mm; the taller back-side speaker and battery socket stand clear of it and no part floats off the board.
contentChecks: The 5 x 5 LED grid is centred on the board, with LED x as column and y as row, origin top-left.
Button A is left and button B right of the LED grid, each with a separate cap that can move.
The gold touch logo is above the LED grid.
Pins 0, 1, 2, 3V and GND are five large rings, left to right, at the edge connector, with gold fingers.
USB connector, reset button, battery socket, speaker and microphone are on the back face of the board.
Every contract part_id exists exactly once, each LED has its own material, and the model carries no BBC or micro:bit logos, FCC ID or text.
